# Character asset audit

**Decision document.** The measurements below are regenerated by
`s32 assets audit`; the **Decision** column is a human judgement and is
preserved by hand.

The governing decision is
`docs/decisions/ADR-0005-character-art-consistency.md`: the central cast comes
from one character system.

## Decisions

| Pack | Score | Role | Decision |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- |
| `pm_char_a01` | — | **CORE** | Adopted. Five free characters, 17 expressions, summer and winter uniforms. |
| `pm_char_a02` | 7.4 | **CORE** | Adopted. Same character system, three casual outfits. Deductions are for saturation and line weight, both explained by casual clothing being more colourful than a uniform — not style drift. Head ratio is identical to three decimal places. |
| `pm_char_nozomi` | 5.1 | candidate | **Not adopted.** The best of the secondaries, and still a 21% line-weight difference and 17% framing difference. Reconsider only for a one-scene background character. |
| `pm_char_keiko` | 3.7 | reject | **Not adopted.** Head ratio 30% larger; line weight 72% heavier. Would read as a different game. |
| `pm_char_kioshi_haruo` | 3.4 | reject | **Not adopted.** The obvious candidate for male characters, and it does not fit: framing 22% different, saturation 43% lower, and 8 of the core's expressions missing. |
| `pm_char_sensei` | 3.4 | reject | **Not adopted.** Head ratio 18% larger, 7 expressions missing. Ms. Ellery stays an art gap rather than a mismatch. |
| `pm_char_hiyori` | 3.4 | reject | **Not adopted.** Line weight 156% heavier — the single largest mismatch measured. |
| `pm_char_ryoko_madoka` | 3.2 | reject | **Not adopted.** Head ratio, framing and line weight all outside tolerance; 8 expressions missing. |
| `pm_char_taishiro` | 3.2 | reject | **Not adopted.** Head ratio 49% larger. Visibly a different style. |

## What the numbers mean

All the secondary packs are by the **same artist** as the core. They still score
between 3.2 and 5.1. That is the finding worth carrying forward: if one
artist's packs differ this much from each other, the intuition that free assets
can be mixed if they "look similar" is simply wrong, and the audit is not
pedantry.

The A02 result is the counter-example that validates the method. It scores 7.4
— not 10 — and the deductions are entirely colour statistics, which is exactly
what you would expect when comparing a school uniform to a casual top. The head
ratio, the thing that actually determines whether two sprites look like the same
person's work, is 0.408 against 0.409.

## Consequences

- **The playable cast is five characters.** iris, theo, mara, june, noah.
- **Ms. Ellery has no sprite.** The Sensei pack exists and does not fit, so she
  is an art gap rather than a compromise. She still speaks.
- **No male-presenting sprite is available** in a compatible style. Recorded in
  `docs/production/ART_GAP_ANALYSIS.md` and open in
  `docs/canon/OPEN_QUESTIONS.md`.
- Secondary packs remain downloaded locally for future reference and are not
  used.

## Method, and its limits

Every figure is computed locally from pixel data. **No image was sent to any
external service** — see `docs/legal/AI_AND_ASSETS_POLICY.md`.

What this cannot tell you: whether two characters look like they belong in the
same school, their apparent age, or their presentation. **Casting was therefore
decided on outfit availability, not appearance** — kohaku and tomomi are the only
free characters present in both A01 and A02, so they went to the two
most-featured roles. A human should review
`tools/reports/contact-sheets/` and recast if the fit is wrong; it is a
one-line edit per character.
